intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the heart of Marrakech at the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Arrive mid-morning to explore the labyrinthine souks of the Medina, visit the Medersa Ben Youssef Islamic school, and end at the square as it transforms into a vibrant open-air spectacle of storytellers, musicians, and food stalls by evening. Staying in a nearby riad ensures you can walk directly to the action without wasting time on transport, especially important given a late Day 1 arrival.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Explore two of Marrakech's most significant historical landmarks within walking distance of each other in the southern Medina. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with intricate tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings, while the Saadian Tombs offer a rare glimpse into the royal necropolis of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty. Book a guided tour for rich historical context. Choosing accommodation in the Kasbah or southern Medina area puts you steps away, making this a perfect half-day activity even after a late arrival the night before.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp at Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Journey to the iconic golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for a sunset camel trek into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, and wake before dawn to witness a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes. To maximize this experience within a 7-day itinerary, take an early morning bus or shared transfer from Marrakech on Day 2 or 3 rather than Day 1, given the late flight arrival. Pre-book a camp located directly at the dune base to avoid extra travel on arrival.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Atlas Mountains Berber Village Hike via Imlil
experiences.description: Take a day trip from Marrakech to the Imlil valley in the High Atlas Mountains, approximately 1.5 hours away. Trek through terraced fields and traditional Berber villages, visit a local family home for mint tea, and enjoy panoramic views of Jebel Toubkal, North Africa's highest peak. This adventure-culture hybrid experience is best scheduled mid-trip when you are already settled in Marrakech. Staying in a riad in the Medina or Gueliz area gives easy access to shared taxis and organized transfers to Imlil each morning.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class in the Medina
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef in a traditional riad kitchen within the Medina. Visit the nearby spice souk to select fresh ingredients including ras el hanout, preserved lemons, and argan oil, then learn to prepare classic dishes such as chicken tagine, harira soup, and msemen flatbread. This is an ideal activity for Day 2 morning after your late Day 1 arrival, requiring no travel outside the Medina. Classes typically run 3 to 4 hours and include a full meal. Booking accommodation inside the Medina walls ensures a 5-minute walk to most class venues.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange a petit taxi or airport bus (Bus 11, ~4 MAD) to Marrakech Boutique Stay in the Medina area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the Marrakech Boutique Stay and freshen up. Take a gentle orientation walk through the nearby streets of the Medina. Stroll along Rue Riad Zitoun el Kedim toward Jemaa el-Fna square to get your bearings. Watch the square come alive with storytellers, musicians, and snake charmers — free entry, just tip performers if you engage.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening soaking up the electric atmosphere of Jemaa el-Fna at dusk. Browse the open-air food stalls (Stall #1 or #32 are popular with locals) for a budget feast of harira soup, grilled meats, and fresh orange juice. Walk back to the riad along the lantern-lit alleys.

meals.breakfast: Eaten on the plane or grab a quick msemen (Moroccan flatbread) with honey from a street vendor near the riad (~5 MAD)
meals.lunch: Quick stop at a local snack stand near the Medina entrance — kefta sandwich or bowl of harira soup (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna night food stalls — grilled brochettes, couscous, and a glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice (~50–70 MAD total)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some euros/dollars to Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina — avoid hotel exchange rates. Keep a small bag of coins for tipping and stall purchases. March weather in Marrakech is mild (15–22°C), so a light jacket for the evening is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims — free). Then head to the Saadian Tombs, a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis (~10 MAD entry). Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat crowds. Afterward, explore the nearby Kasbah neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (30 MAD entry), a lavish 19th-century palace with beautiful zellij tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Spend 1–1.5 hours exploring its 150 rooms. Then wander through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to see the historic synagogues and colorful balconies — free to walk through.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna for sunset views from a rooftop café (Café de France or Café Argana — order a mint tea ~15 MAD for the view). Explore the souks of the Medina by night — Souk Semmarine and Souk el Attarine are magical after dark. Practice your bargaining skills!

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the riad or a local café — Moroccan mint tea, msemen, olive oil, and amlou (almond-argan dip) (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Chez Bahia or a local darj near Bahia Palace — tagine of the day with bread (~40–55 MAD)
meals.dinner: Earth Café (vegetarian-friendly, budget-friendly) near the Medina or another small local restaurant in the souks (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs can have queues — go early. Wear modest clothing (shoulders and knees covered) out of cultural respect, especially near mosques. Bargaining in the souks is expected — start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (70 MAD entry), one of the most beautiful Islamic schools in North Africa, dating to the 14th century. Marvel at the intricate stucco, zellij tiles, and carved cedar woodwork. Then explore the surrounding northern Medina neighborhood and the ancient Almoravid Koubba (20 MAD), the oldest standing monument in Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Marrakech Museum (Dar Menebhi Palace, 50 MAD) housed in a stunning 19th-century palace — exhibits on Moroccan art and history. Afterward, get lost in the Dyers' Souk (Souk des Teinturiers) to see wool being dyed in vibrant colors — a fantastic free spectacle. Visit the Spice Square (Rahba Kedima) for aromatic herbs and traditional remedies.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free Gnawa music performance in Jemaa el-Fna (most evenings after 8 PM). Dine at a local hole-in-the-wall restaurant in the Medina for an authentic Moroccan meal. End the night with a walk through the quieter, lamp-lit alleys near your riad.

meals.breakfast: Msemen, honey, and mint tea at a local café near Ben Youssef Madrasa (~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant near the northern Medina — vegetable couscous or lentil soup with bread (~35–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Haj Boujemaa or similar local eatery near Jemaa el-Fna — kefta tagine with khobz bread (~55–70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: A combined ticket for Ben Youssef Madrasa + Marrakech Museum + Almoravid Koubba is available (~120 MAD) — good value. Carry a small water bottle; March afternoons can be warm. The Dyers' Souk is most active in the morning hours.

day_by_day.morning: Depart very early (around 6:00–7:00 AM) by shared CTM or Supratours bus toward Ouarzazate and onward to Merzouga/Sahara (total journey ~9–10 hours by shared transport, ~150–200 MAD). Alternatively, join a budget group tour departing from Marrakech (from ~600–800 MAD for a 2-day/1-night Sahara trip including transport and basic camp). Watch the dramatic landscape shift from the High Atlas Mountains through the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) to the Draa Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Draa Valley or continue toward Merzouga. Stop at Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) that has appeared in Game of Thrones and Gladiator — walk through the ancient earthen towers (~10 MAD suggested donation). Continue through Ouarzazate, the 'Hollywood of Africa,' and its kasbah.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga as the sun sets. Mount a camel for a short sunset ride into the Sahara (~100–150 MAD for a short ride). Settle into a basic desert camp (included in group tour or book separately ~200–300 MAD for a bed in a shared Berber tent). Enjoy a campfire, traditional Berber music, and a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure — bread, jam, and tea (~free or 20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop en route — tagine at a roadside café near Ouarzazate (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — vegetable tagine, couscous, and mint tea (usually included in camp package or ~80–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara transport and camp in advance — shared buses or group tours fill up quickly in March (spring travel season). Pack a warm layer — desert nights drop to 5–8°C in March. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, and a scarf/shemagh for sand protection. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (around 5:30 AM) to watch the sunrise over the Erg Chebbi dunes — one of the most spectacular sights in Morocco. Climb a dune for panoramic views of the golden sea of sand. Take a short morning walk or sandboard down the dunes (boards sometimes available at camp). Return to camp for a Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the village of Merzouga on foot — visit the local market and interact with the Berber community. Optional: visit a nomadic family camp nearby (arranged through your tour guide, free or small tip). Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via shared transport or group tour vehicle, passing through the Ziz Valley and the stunning Todra Gorge if the route allows.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening (around 9–10 PM depending on route). Check back into the riad. Grab a late snack from a street vendor near the riad — a simple bowl of harira or a sandwich — and rest for the night.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — flatbread, olive oil, honey, dates, and mint tea (included in camp or ~30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside café lunch en route — harira soup, bread, and a Coke (~35–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near the riad in Marrakech — harira, bissara (fava bean soup), or a kefta sandwich (~30–40 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long — bring snacks, water, and entertainment. If you have extra budget (~100–150 MAD more), stopping at the Todra Gorge adds a spectacular detour. Keep your belongings secure during bus travel. Rest well tonight — two more days of Marrakech exploration ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (70 MAD entry) — a stunning botanical garden created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Stroll among cobalt-blue buildings, exotic cacti, and lily ponds. Also visit the small Berber Museum within the garden (included in ticket). Arrive early to avoid weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah market and Souk Cherifa for unique artisan goods and souvenirs — handmade leather goods, argan oil, pottery, and Berber jewelry. This is your best day for thoughtful, budget-friendly souvenir shopping (bargain respectfully). Visit the El Badi Palace ruins (20 MAD) — a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now in atmospheric ruin, with resident storks nesting on the towers.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional hammam experience at a local public hammam (Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a neighborhood hammam ~20–50 MAD for basic entry + kessa scrub). This is a quintessential Moroccan cultural experience. End the evening with a final wander through Jemaa el-Fna and a sit-down dinner at a slightly nicer budget restaurant to celebrate your last full day.

meals.breakfast: Café Kif Kif or a riad café near Majorelle Garden — avocado toast or Moroccan breakfast (~30–40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café Clock Marrakech (near the Medina) — famous camel burger or vegetarian options (~60–80 MAD, a worthwhile splurge)
meals.dinner: Le Jardin restaurant (budget section) or Nomad Restaurant for modern Moroccan cuisine — 2-course meal (~80–120 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is one of Marrakech's most popular attractions — book tickets online in advance if possible to avoid queues. Saturday markets are lively and colorful. For the hammam, bring flip-flops and a change of clothes. Tipping the hammam attendant (~10–20 MAD) is customary.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the lively Mellah Sunday Market or the weekly Berber market at Place des Ferblantiers for last-minute authentic souvenirs and local atmosphere. Enjoy a leisurely Moroccan breakfast at your riad or a nearby café. Pick up some argan oil, ras el hanout spice mix, or dried roses as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last stroll through the Medina — revisit your favorite spots. If time allows, visit the Museum of Confluences (Dar Si Said, ~30 MAD) for a beautiful collection of Moroccan decorative arts, Berber jewelry, and historic carpets. Begin packing and prepare for departure. Check out of the riad (standard checkout is 12:00 PM — arrange luggage storage if needed).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with ample time (allow 2–2.5 hours before departure). Take Bus 11 or a negotiated petit taxi (~50–80 MAD to airport). Enjoy a final mint tea at the airport and reflect on an incredible week in Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at the riad or a café — msemen, honey, amlou, and mint tea (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Medina café or street food — merguez sandwich or briouates (fried pastries with cheese/meat) (~25–40 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport café or a final street food snack before departure — or eat on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time to reach the airport on Sundays — traffic near the Medina can be unpredictable. Keep some MAD for last-minute tips, porter fees, or airport snacks. Leftover dirhams can be exchanged back at the airport (keep your exchange receipts). Morocco has a 10 MAD airport departure tax sometimes charged separately — confirm with your airline.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Marrakech Boutique Stay in the Medina (~20–30 min by taxi, ~100–150 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your riad.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the nearby souks and lanes of the Medina. Stroll to Jemaa el-Fna square to absorb the atmosphere — snake charmers, musicians, and juice stalls. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior) for a classic first Marrakech photo.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner on a rooftop terrace overlooking Jemaa el-Fna. Watch the square transform into a massive open-air food market with dozens of stalls. Enjoy a leisurely mint tea at a café balcony as the city comes alive.

meals.breakfast: Skipped / light snack on the plane
meals.lunch: Fresh-squeezed orange juice and a sandwich or msemen (Moroccan flatbread) from a stall near Jemaa el-Fna (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant such as Le Marrakchi or a similar mid-range spot overlooking the square — tagine or couscous with harira soup (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange currency at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina (avoid hotel rates). Dress modestly when exploring the Medina.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Bahia Palace (built late 19th century) — a stunning example of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture with intricate zellij tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Then walk to the nearby Badi Palace ruins for a contrast of grandeur and decay (~20 MAD entry each).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saadian Tombs, a beautifully preserved royal necropolis from the 16th century (~70 MAD). Afterward, dive into the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to explore its distinctive architecture and the covered Mellah market. Stop at the Maison de la Photographie for a curated look at historical Morocco through photography (~50 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Attend an authentic Gnawa music performance at a cultural center or riad venue — a powerful spiritual music tradition indigenous to Morocco. Then wander back through the illuminated Jemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Moroccan breakfast at your riad or a nearby café — msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, olives, and mint tea (~50–80 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in the Mellah — bissara (fava bean soup) and bread (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nomad Restaurant in the Medina — modern Moroccan cuisine in a stylish rooftop setting (~180–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are uneven cobblestone. A local guide for the palaces and tombs (~200–300 MAD for a half-day) can greatly enrich the historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum complex — arrive early to beat crowds. The cobalt-blue garden designed by Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent is iconic (~150 MAD garden entry, ~300 MAD combined with museum). Explore the Berber Museum within the complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the vibrant souks of the Medina — spice souk, leather tanneries (view from a terrace above), lantern souk, and textile souk. Practice your bargaining skills. Stop at a traditional hammam (public bathhouse) for a 1-hour scrub and steam session — a deeply cultural and relaxing experience (~150–250 MAD at a mid-range hammam).
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class at a local riad — learn to make a traditional Moroccan tagine, couscous, and pastilla. This doubles as your dinner and is a highlight cultural experience (~400–600 MAD per person including meal).

meals.breakfast: Café des Épices or similar café near the spice square — café au lait, croissant, and fresh juice (~60–80 MAD)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a food stall in the souks — merguez sandwich or kefta wrap (~30–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in the cooking class experience

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam and cooking class in advance — popular spots fill up quickly. The hammam is a must-do cultural experience; bring a swimsuit or wear underwear. Majorelle Garden opens at 8:00 AM — arriving at opening avoids crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (~6:00–7:00 AM) by private transfer or shared minibus toward Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley — this is the start of the Sahara journey. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260 m) in the High Atlas for panoramic views and photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ouarzazate (~4 hrs from Marrakech). Visit the Kasbah Taourirt — a UNESCO-recognized earthen fortress (~20 MAD). Optional short visit to the Atlas Film Studios, one of the world's largest film studios where Game of Thrones and Gladiator were filmed (~80 MAD). Continue driving toward the Draa Valley through stunning palm oases.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp or guesthouse near Zagora or Mhamid (~2–3 hrs from Ouarzazate). Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under the stars around a campfire with live music.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad in Marrakech before departure — packed or quick café stop on the road
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in or near Ouarzazate — tagine of lamb with prunes (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included at the desert camp — traditional Berber couscous or tagine with mint tea (~150–200 MAD if not included)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~8–10 hrs total with stops) — pack snacks and water. Book a reputable desert camp in advance; mid-range options offer comfortable Berber tents with proper bedding and shared bathrooms. Sunset from the desert is spectacular — arrive before dusk.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise for a camel trek into the Sahara dunes (Erg Chegaga or Erg Lihoudi depending on location). Watch the sunrise over the dunes — one of the most memorable moments of the trip. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: 4x4 desert excursion through the Draa Valley — visit ancient ksour (fortified villages), fossil beds, and remote oases. Learn about desert survival and Berber nomadic traditions from your guide. Optional sandboarding on the dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for sunset. Stargazing session — the Sahara has virtually zero light pollution, making it one of the best places on Earth to observe the night sky. Sleep in the desert camp for a second night (optional) or begin the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at camp — flatbread, olive oil, amlou, dates, and mint tea (included in camp stay)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the camp in the desert — sandwiches, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at camp around the fire — tagine, salads, and fresh bread (~included or ~150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Temperatures in March are ideal — warm days (~25°C) and cool nights (~10°C). Bring a light jacket or fleece for evenings. Protect camera equipment from sand. The camel trek is typically 1–2 hours each way and is suitable for beginners.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert camp and begin the return journey toward Marrakech via a different scenic route — through the Dades Gorge and Todra Gorge. Stop at Todra Gorge — dramatic 300-meter-high canyon walls, popular with rock climbers. Short hike along the gorge floor (~1–2 km, easy).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) — famous for its Damask roses harvested each spring. In March, early blooms may already be visible. Stop at a local cooperative to learn about rose water and argan oil production. Drive through the scenic Skoura palm grove.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech (~late afternoon/early evening). Check back into your boutique riad. Relax with a hammam session or simply rest. Light dinner near the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the desert camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Tinghir near Todra Gorge — mixed Moroccan salads and tagine (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a Medina restaurant near your riad — harira soup, kefta tagine, and Moroccan pastries (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: This is another long driving day (~7–9 hrs with stops). The Dades and Todra gorge route is more scenic than the outbound road — highly recommended. Confirm your riad reservation is still active for the return night. March is the beginning of rose season — timing is excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — revisit any missed sights or simply enjoy a slow breakfast at your riad. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (Islamic school from the 14th century, reopened after restoration) — one of the most beautifully decorated buildings in all of Morocco (~70 MAD). Browse the Rahba Lakdima (spice square) for last-minute souvenirs — saffron, argan oil, rose water, and Berber spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping in the souks for gifts — leather goods, lanterns, ceramics, or handwoven textiles. Enjoy a final mint tea and pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) at a traditional café. Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure (allow 2 hrs before flight).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Reflect on an incredible week of kasbahs, souks, mountain passes, and Sahara sunrises.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the riad — the full Moroccan spread with all the classics (~50–80 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Clock or a similar well-regarded mid-range spot — camel burger (a Marrakech specialty), salads, and fresh juice (~120–160 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time at the airport — Marrakech Menara can be busy. Pack purchases carefully — argan oil must be in checked luggage if over 100ml. Keep some MAD for airport tips or last purchases. The Ben Youssef Madrasa is best visited early before tour groups arrive. This is a wonderful final morning activity.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Marrakech Boutique Stay in a chauffeured vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into the boutique riad. Enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony in the hotel's courtyard. Take a gentle orientation stroll through the nearby lanes of the medina to acclimatize — explore the vibrant souks around Mouassine quarter at your own pace, browsing artisan leather goods, spices, and lanterns.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset rooftop aperitif at the hotel terrace overlooking the medina rooftops and Atlas Mountains silhouette. Dinner at a prestigious riad restaurant in the medina — recommended: La Maison Arabe or Dar Yacout — for an immersive Moroccan feast of pastilla, slow-cooked tagine, and honey-drenched pastries in a candlelit courtyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (afternoon arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome mezze and refreshments arranged by the hotel upon check-in
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout or La Maison Arabe — a multi-course traditional Moroccan banquet with live Gnawa music; budget MAD 600–900 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance with the hotel's concierge. Request a late check-in if needed. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Dress modestly for medina exploration — light layers recommended for March evenings which can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Koutoubia Mosque gardens, followed by an expert-led visit to the stunning Bahia Palace — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture with intricately carved cedarwood ceilings and mosaic courtyards. Continue to the atmospheric ruins of El Badi Palace, once considered one of the world's most magnificent courts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive private visit to the Saadian Tombs — ornate royal mausoleums discovered in 1917, adorned with Italian Carrara marble and Zellij tilework. Afterward, explore the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) with your guide, visiting the old synagogue and spice market. Wind down with a curated souk shopping experience guided by a local artisan expert — custom-select handmade leather babouches, argan oil products, and Berber rugs.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam and spa ritual at a premium riad hammam (e.g., Heritage Spa or Les Bains de Marrakech) — black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Dinner at Nomad Marrakech rooftop restaurant — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with panoramic medina views.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Moroccan breakfast at the hotel — msemen flatbreads, amlou almond-argan dip, fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan coffee, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a hidden medina restaurant — harira soup, briouats, and couscous with seven vegetables
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nomad Marrakech — modern Moroccan plates including lamb mechoui and bastilla au lait; budget MAD 400–700 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam session in advance as premium slots fill quickly. Hire a licensed private guide (MAD 400–600/half day) for palace visits to gain deeper historical context. Wear comfortable walking shoes for medina exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Private day excursion to the Ourika Valley in the High Atlas Mountains (45-minute luxury drive from Marrakech). Visit a traditional Berber village with a local guide — learn about mountain life, agricultural terraces, and ancient irrigation systems. Trek gently along the Ourika River to the seven-tiered Setti Fatma waterfalls (moderate hike, approximately 45 minutes up).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return partway and stop at a family-run Berber cooperative for a private argan oil and rose water production demonstration. Enjoy a scenic lunch in the valley. On the return drive, visit the Anima Garden — André Heller's extraordinary private sculpture garden blooming with exotic plants and contemporary art installations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by late afternoon. Freshen up at the hotel. Experience Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk — watch storytellers, acrobats, and snake charmers as the square transforms into a living theatre. Dinner at Le Tobsil — a legendary Moroccan fine dining experience inside a candlelit 17th-century riad with a fixed prix-fixe menu of 12 traditional courses.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Authentic Berber lunch at a local mountain restaurant in Ourika Valley — tagine cooked over charcoal, fresh salads, and mint tea with Atlas spring water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Tobsil — prix-fixe 12-course Moroccan feast; approximately MAD 700–900 per person including wine

day_by_day.notes: Atlas Mountain roads can be winding — motion sickness tablets recommended if sensitive. March weather in the valley may be cooler; bring a light jacket. Book Le Tobsil well in advance as it is consistently fully reserved. Anima Garden charges a small entry fee.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the epic journey to the Sahara Desert (approximately 8–9 hours total with scenic stops). First stop: the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas — breathtaking panoramic vistas and snow-dusted peaks in March. Stop at a roadside Berber market for local honey and fossils.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley — a lush corridor of palm groves, kasbahs, and ancient ksour (fortified villages). Visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — a spectacular 11th-century earthen ksar used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Guided exploration of its labyrinthine alleyways and granaries with a local historian.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the Sahara desert camp near Merzouga or Zagora (depending on route). Mount private camels at sunset for a guided dune trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp — private Berber-style tent with en-suite bathroom, plush furnishings, and stargazing terrace. Dinner under a sky blazing with stars around a private campfire with traditional musicians.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — packed pastries and fruit provided for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant in Ouarzazate or near Aït Benhaddou — mechoui lamb and Moroccan salads
meals.dinner: Private camp dinner — slow-cooked lamb tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and traditional desserts served in your luxury tent; included in camp package

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — depart no later than 07:30. Hire a professional driver-guide who knows the route well. Ensure the luxury desert camp is pre-booked (recommended: Luxury Berber Camp Erg Chebbi or similar 5-star camp). Pack warm clothing — Sahara nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring a good camera for the dunes at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise for a private sunrise camel ride or guided dune hike to the crest of the highest dune for a panoramic Sahara sunrise — one of the most breathtaking experiences in Morocco. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional sandboarding or quad biking on the dunes (arrange through the camp). Visit a local nomadic Tuareg family encampment for authentic tea and cultural exchange.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the desert and begin the scenic return journey. Stop at the Tafilalt Oasis — the largest oasis in Morocco — for a guided palm grove walk and exploration of the ancient Sijilmassa ruins, once the starting point of trans-Saharan gold and salt trade routes. Continue to Erfoud, famous for its trilobite and ammonite fossil workshops — visit a family-run fossil atelier.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a luxury kasbah hotel in the Draa or Ziz Valley (e.g., Kasbah Ait Ben Moro or Kasbah Xaluca) — a beautifully restored fortified palace with pool and garden. Dinner at the kasbah's private restaurant — slow-roasted mechoui and Moroccan wine selection on a candlelit terrace.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the desert camp — fresh bread, eggs, Moroccan pancakes, honey, and argan oil
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Erfoud or Rissani — harira, kefta tagine, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at the kasbah restaurant — traditional Moroccan menu with premium wine pairing; approximately MAD 500–800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Set an alarm for 05:30 to catch the optimal sunrise. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf for desert wind. The fossil workshops in Erfoud are fascinating but be aware of tourist pricing — negotiate respectfully. Confirm kasbah reservation before departing the desert camp.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the kasbah — enjoy the pool, hammam, or garden before departing. Begin the scenic drive back toward Marrakech via a different route through the Roses Valley (Vallée des Roses) near El Kelaa M'Gouna — in March, early rose buds may be appearing ahead of the April festival. Visit a rose water distillery and cooperative to see how Moroccan rose products are made.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dadès Gorge — dramatic red-rock canyon with towering cliffs and winding roads nicknamed the 'Road of a Thousand Kasbahs.' Stop for photography at the famous hairpin bends. Visit the Skoura palm grove and the 17th-century Kasbah Amerhidil. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Marrakech Boutique Stay. Indulge in a private in-room spa treatment or rooftop jacuzzi session. Farewell dinner at a world-class restaurant — recommended: Al Fassia Aguedal (women-run, legendary Moroccan cuisine) or the rooftop of Café de la Poste for French-Moroccan fusion — celebrate the journey with a bottle of Moroccan Gris de Boulaouane wine.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the kasbah hotel before checkout
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch prepared by the kasbah to enjoy at a scenic Dadès Gorge viewpoint, or a quick stop at a local roadside tagine house
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Al Fassia Aguedal — refined traditional Moroccan cuisine in an elegant garden setting; MAD 500–800 per person

day_by_day.notes: The drive from the kasbah to Marrakech is approximately 5–6 hours with stops — depart by 09:00. The Dadès Gorge hairpin section is best photographed in afternoon light. If time allows, a brief stop at Ait Benhaddou from a different angle on the return is worthwhile. Confirm dinner reservation before leaving in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum, the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden designed by Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Stroll through the garden's exotic cacti, bamboo groves, and reflecting pools. The adjacent Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech houses stunning fashion retrospectives and rotating art exhibitions — a must for design and culture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute curated shopping in the Gueliz district (new town) — visit contemporary Moroccan design boutiques, galleries, and concept stores for high-quality souvenirs: handcrafted ceramics, Berber jewelry, and luxury leather goods. Enjoy a final mint tea and pastilla at a café terrace. Private transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech — carry the memories of the medina's labyrinthine alleys, the vast silence of the Sahara, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final lavish Moroccan breakfast at the hotel — a celebratory spread of msemen, beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), fresh juices, Moroccan coffee, and seasonal fruit platter
meals.lunch: Brunch or light lunch at Café du Livre or Kechmara in Gueliz — French-Moroccan bistro fare with excellent coffee and pastries
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining (departure dependent on flight time)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden opens at 08:00 — arriving early avoids crowds. Book YSL Museum tickets online in advance as they frequently sell out. Allow at least 3 hours before flight for airport check-in. Settle any hotel extras and tip staff generously — tipping culture is important in Morocco (MAD 50–100 per day for hotel staff is customary at luxury properties). Ensure all purchased goods are properly packaged for travel, especially ceramics and leather items.
